newsitem.title: USA: IBP to buy Foodbrands for $640 mln.
newsitem.headline: IBP to buy Foodbrands for $640 mln.

text.p: U.S. meat producer IBP Inc said Wednesday it had agreed to buy Foodbrands America Inc for $23.40 cash per share in a transaction valued at $640 million, including Foodbrands debt.
Foodbrands makes, markets and distributes frozen and refrigerated products to the away-from-home food preparation market, the companies said.
IBP said the acquisition will increase its presence in the foodservice industry, advance its strategy of diversifying beyond the core fresh meat processing business, and extended its product base.
IBP said that on April 1 it would commence a cash tender offer for the 12.47 million Foodbrands shares outstanding.
Foodbrands's largest shareholders, Joseph Littlejohn and Levy Ltd Partnerships, which together own about 44 percent of Foodbrands's stock, have agreed to tender their shares, IBP said.
The next largest Foodbrands shareholder, Airlie Group, has also agreed to tender, the company said.
"We have been exploring ways to capitalize on the trend by Americans of spending more on food prepared outside the home than on groceries to prepare at home," IBP Chairman Robert Peterson said.

"The addition of Foodbrands's business is a perfect complement to IBP's core processing business and will allow us to further extend our reach into restaurants and supermarket deli cases with high-quality branded products."
IBP said it intended to operate Foodbrands as a largely independent business, bringing its 3,300 managers and employees into IBP.
The transaction has been approved by the boards of both companies and is expected to close in the second quarter, the companies said. The deal is subject to certain regulatory approvals, they said.

Foodbrands, based in Oklahoma City, produces over 1,600 branded and custom products, including pizza toppings and crusts, burritos, frozen stuffed pastas, breaded appetizers, soups, sauces and side dishes, as well as deli meats and processed beef, poultry and pork. Its customers include restaurant chains, foodservice distributors, warehouse clubs and grocery store delicatessens.
